主要内容: Portugal's Defense Ministry budget was US$3.14 billion in 2012, recording a CAGR of 1.7% during the review period. The Portuguese government faces economic constraints due to high fiscal debt, expected to reach 115% of GDP by 2013, and is projected to reduce it to 4.5% of GDP by 2017 through austerity measures. These measures include extending t-bill maturities and cutting defense spending. The government has cut the 2006 military funding program (LPM) budget by 40% until 2013 and will not make new military equipment purchases until 2013. Portugal's homeland security budget stood at US$2.2 billion in 2012, with a CAGR of -3.08% during the review period, but is expected to grow at 7.68% to reach US$3.01 billion by 2017. Defense imports declined sharply in 2011, reaching 115% of 2010 levels, and are expected to continue declining due to austerity measures. The LPM program included purchases of submarines, frigates, aircraft, and armored vehicles, but funding cuts will limit future acquisitions. Companies mentioned include OGMA, Indústria Aeronáutica de Portugal SA, EID, ENVC, Indra Sistemas Portugal, AgustaWestland Portugal, and others.
